opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita Young (E001) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the Payroll Specialist role owns the Payroll system, the full_time policy permits admin access. Recommend granting admin to Payroll as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E001 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never receive admin; max for basic-trained contractor is read. Recommend granting read to Payroll (requested admin exceeds max). Note: this conflicts with HR's note claiming full-time status.
reason: There is a conflict: HR's note lists E001 as full-time (which would permit admin since Payroll Specialist owns Payroll), but Security's note lists E001 as a contractor with basic security training (which limits access to read and never admin). Given the conflicting employment-type records, I apply the more restrictive verified policy: contractors never receive admin, and a basic-trained contractor's maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds this maximum, so I grant the maximum allowable level, read.
